findings.what: The platform-parity half of the rubric row has no evidence anywhere in the set. All 18 region reports under evidence/logs/*.report.json record platform 'a browser'; MANIFEST.json records browser 'webkit' for the whole capture; frames.json records source 'webkit' and scroll_emulator {missing: 'no Android device was up in this session'}; coldstart.json's two tailscale nodes are both os 'linux'. Two of the seventeen artifacts are absent and they are exactly the two that would have shown the Android build. The reason recorded in WHY_MISSING.json is a standing machine fact (no /dev/kvm, adbd answering after 113 minutes with no framework behind it, no GTK for a desktop stand-in) and logs/apk.json shows a real 101.2 MB arm64 release APK signed with a non-debug key, so the reason is a reason and not an excuse.
findings.why: The row's own words are 'both platforms serve the same regions, the same feelings, and the same event types from the one codebase'. The same event renders in the same language in three regions. 'the second one - the place by the bridge', 'sunday 9 call KEPT', 'text when home KEPT' and 'the one you said you stopped - PASSED ON' all appear in 03_us.png as module rows and again in crops/04_moments_what_happened.png as milestone-lens rows; 'text when home KEPT' appears a third time as a ritual_kept row inside the Chat thread in 02_chat.png at y 1280-1520.

not_worth_opening.path: evidence/logs/torn.json, flat.json, holes.json, lines.json, grain.json, tears.json, hairline.json, surfaces.json, hand.json, fonts.json
not_worth_opening.why: These measure the paper, the tear profile, the contact shadow, the ruling pitch and the hand's repeat rate. They belong to the material row. My row asks whether the ten artifacts read as one system, and for that I compared the surfaces directly across regions and lighting conditions rather than through these files. The one place I would have used them - whether type falls off its own sheet - none of them measures, which is why that finding is taken from pixels.

The derivation of the felt-distance floor and the per-pattern separability numbers are the emotional-transmission row's. I opened crops/haptics_strip.png instead, because what my row needs from the vocabulary is whether authored feelings sit in the same families and the same table as built-ins, which the strip shows and the JSON would only restate.

A test log is the code reader's evidence, not a captured artifact, and BRIEFING.md is explicit that the code half of row 04 stays inside the builder's own score. Reading it would be scoring my row on something a critic is not given.
The feeling's sound track is the emotional row's; nothing about whether the regions are one system turns on it. I did use frames.json and the clip frame counts for the length finding.

evidence/frames.json already carries every field these repeat - step_ms, app_seconds, playback_over_app_time, the held-frame thresholds and the repeated-frame counts - and I read it in full, so opening the per-clip duplicates would add nothing.

verdict: The set shows one system far more than it shows an assembly, and the parts of my row that can be measured from artifacts mostly hold: the standing line carrying partner state is bit-identical across all eight seeded stills and now reaches 14_media_viewer, which was the one screen missing it; the same five module items render in the same hand and the same chip grammar in Us, in the Moments milestone lens and - for rituals, to-dos and dates - inline in the Chat thread; a fifth module, the shelf, sits in the shared module scaffolding with its own event type and turns up unmodified in search and in the archive, which is the clearest extensibility evidence the set has ever had to offer; the two authored feelings sit in the same families and the same haptic table as the 34 built-ins; and the dusk condition is a real transform (desk luma down 52 percent, paper down 13 percent and warmed) rather than a tint. What holds the row below its floor is that Chat, the region that is supposed to be the full rendering of the spine, demonstrably is not: in 13_messenger_states.png four of the seven message rows the app's own log places in the viewport paint nothing across a continuous 1480-pixel band that is 47.4 percent of the frame and 0.0152 percent paper, and the rows that vanished are the refusal, the delivered reply and two sent notes - the exact states the artifact exists to prove. That is the blocking finding. Behind it sits the same fault in motion in 08_state_propagating.mp4, where three of four message rows hold 0.65 percent ink to the last frame, and a systemic regression in which type is laid out without regard to how much paper survives the tear - chip sheets in 12_search.png lost 31 to 49 percent of their area while the words did not shrink, and the hero's ritual title and voice-note timestamp are now cut by their own edges. Two clauses of the row I could not judge at all: nothing captured from the Android build exists anywhere in the set - every one of the eighteen region reports says platform 'a browser' - and the stills, clips and reception scene are shot at three different logical widths, at two of which the partner's status line truncates. The repair that would move this row most is one change: commit a row's paper, its mask and its ink together, and lay the ink inside what the mask leaves, rather than painting the sheet first and the words afterwards on whatever is left.
